title: Audit Console: anchored time-window query builder with resumable export checkpoints and role-aware masking
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add an advanced query experience for the Audit Console that supports: anchored time-window queries (start anchored at a chosen event/time and sliding windows for stable pagination), resumable CSV/JSON exports via export checkpoints, role-aware field masking based on RBAC v2, parameterized saved queries, and deterministic cursor pagination. This ticket covers backend APIs, indexing recommendations, and the minimal console UI for selecting anchors / resuming exports. Goals: allow on-call and security teams to reliably run large historical exports (days/weeks of events) without re-scanning results after transient failures; ensure PII fields are masked in exported artifacts according to RBAC v2 rules; and provide predictable performance (bounded memory / shard-friendly scans).
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint GET /audit/query that accepts anchor_time, window_size, filters, role_token and returns a stable cursor that can be used for pagination
POST /audit/exports creates an export job capturing the query + RBAC context and returns an export_id with resumable checkpoint tokens
Export worker resumes from checkpoint tokens so cancelled/failed exports restart without duplicating rows
Exports support CSV and JSONL (NDJSON) formats and adhere to role-aware masking rules defined by RBAC v2 policies
Saved queries may include parameter placeholders (time offsets, user ids) and can be run with a chosen anchor_time
UI displays export progress with checkpoint timestamps and allows resuming or revoking an in-progress export
Performance: a single export worker should stream at least 20 MB/s on a heavy tenant dataset without exceeding 4GB memory
Security review completed and KMS/HSM audit for any persisted export artifacts verified
E2E tests cover masking combinations and at-least-once resume semantics (no duplicates after resume)
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Created ticket with feature sketch after tabletop with SOC. Emphasized need for checkpoints to avoid OOMs during multi-day exports.

2026-02-24 Diego Fernandes: Spike complete. Prototype uses time-indexed shards and a small per-export checkpoint blob stored in tenant metastore (export_id -> last_emitted_event_id). Found that naive prefix scanning causes hot shards for very active tenants.

2026-03-02 Diego Fernandes: Decision: use anchored window + bounded backfill (window_size default 6h) and allow sliding to support arbitrary range exports; this reduces hot-shard pressure vs scanning unbounded ranges. Tradeoff: exported snapshots for extremely-wide ranges will produce more checkpoint handoffs but keep worker memory bounded.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair (Security): Requested RBAC v2 matrix mapping events -> sensitive fields and recommended masking levels (redact, hash, omit). Added security-review_required flag. Need to include SSO/SAML assertion correlation (session_id) in exports when allowed.

2026-03-06 Gabe Ortiz (Infra): Raised concern about NDJSON streaming semantics and idempotency. Suggested adding monotonic event sequence numbers to each event to allow resume de-duplication on consumer side. We will add sequence_id to export metadata.

2026-03-08 Diego Fernandes: WIP PR open: github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/4201 (backend export checkpointing and cursor schema). Need review from infra and security. Also added confluence design link below.

2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to include performance target and E2E tests. Set due_date to 2026-03-15 to align with release planning. Noted UI work will be follow-up ticket for advanced visualization of resumed ranges.
